transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Friday, November 6. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. LAL salaam: Two largest US cities now run by PIOs. Like Mamdani in New York, Nithya Raman is a Leftist Democrat 'You'll know soon enough': Trump's warning on 'destroying' rest of Iran. During a press conference at the Oval Office, Donald Trump cautioned Iran regarding its nuclear ambitions, hinting at possible future actions while preferring to avoid escalation. He asserted that Iran must seek US approval for any developments in its nuclear program, showcasing America's ongoing influence. These statements highlight the escalating tensions and complex dynamics between the two nations. Wall Street bloodbath: $2.5 trillion wiped out as Nasdaq suffers worst crash in 18 months. Wall Street faced a dramatic selloff with technology stocks plummeting due to growing concerns about artificial intelligence spending. Investors reevaluated popular AI-related trades after midterm election results suggested potential tougher scrutiny in the industry. The Nasdaq dropped more than 5 percent , marking its worst session in 18 months and entering correction territory. The selloff spread to Asian markets, leading to declines in Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's Kospi. 'Vote red today!' Elon Musk deletes pro-Republican posts after spending $458 million. Elon Musk removed social media posts encouraging support for Republican candidates after Democrats achieved significant victories. His pinned message included a call to vote Republican on Election Day. Musk's financial backing totaled around $458 million, making him a significant donor during the election cycle. The election results also caused a decline in Musk's personal wealth and the stock values of his companies. Uber shares one number to tell everyone, how 'unpopular' AI Agents may be on its platform. Tech companies have heavily invested in the development of autonomous AI agents for everyday tasks. However, Uber's recent earnings report revealed very few AI-hailed rides during a busy week. Similarly, DoorDash reported only a few hundred AI-initiated orders, emphasizing user preference for native apps. Uber's CEO noted that current booking efficiency reduces the need for AI applications. 'Ordinary bowler': Ex-cricketer slams CSK's 'confusing' trade, says SRH real winners. Kris Srikkanth has raised concerns regarding Chennai Super Kings' recent trades involving Liam Livingstone and Jack Edwards. He contends that Sunrisers Hyderabad emerged as the true winners of the four-player exchange ahead of the IPL 2027 auction. Srikkanth examined Livingstone's potential role in CSK's squad and expressed skepticism over acquiring Edwards, noting that existing overseas talents may hinder Livingstone's chances, ultimately favoring Sunrisers Hyderabad in the deal. Delhi woman, 24, chased phone snatchers 500m, got them caught. In a courageous act near Shalimar Bagh Metro Station, Khushi Maheshwari chased down two men who attempted to steal her iPhone. Despite falling from her scooty during the pursuit, she received support from local residents and police. The suspects were quickly apprehended, with Khushi's phone and other stolen items recovered, emphasizing how crucial community solidarity is for maintaining public safety. Massive fire breaks out at shop in Delhi's Karol Bagh, 22 fire tenders deployed. A significant fire occurred in a commercial building located in Delhi's Gaffar Market, affecting mobile accessory shops. The fire started in a ground-floor shop where mobile batteries were stored, resulting in widespread damage. Emergency services, including 20-25 fire tenders, were dispatched promptly to manage the situation. Fortunately, no casualties or injuries have been reported, with only property damage noted. Indian-American Harmeet Dhillon quits as US civil rights chief after midterm poll rout. After the US midterm elections, Harmeet Kaur Dhillon has stepped down as head of the Civil Rights Division. Her leadership was marked by a reorientation towards diversity initiatives and university admissions policies. Attorney General Todd Blanche endorsed her efforts to uphold civil liberties, yet faced pushback due to workforce reductions within the division. Dhillon's exit also reflects a growing trend of Indian-origin leaders shaping American governance. Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam move Supreme Court for bail. Referring to the contradictory orders given by Supreme Court in the matter of bail to the accused on the ground of delay in trial and long incarceration for UAPA offences, which have been referred to a larger bench for authoritative pronouncement, former student activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam have moved SC for bail in 2020 Delhi riots cases. Kanye West's 6,713-acre Wyoming ranch bought back by family that once owned it. In 2019, Kanye West acquired the Bighorn Mountain Ranch, visualizing it as an exclusive retreat. However, with shifting priorities, the Flitner family reacquired the property in 2025. Concerns over potential subdivision led them to prioritize agricultural preservation and landscape protection, ensuring that historic structures could be restored and serve as a lasting connection to the land for future generations. Michigan neighbours' $2,000 tree dispute ends as court blocks fresh lawsuit. Two Michigan neighbours agreed to pay $2,000 each to remove trees that threatened a barn, but the work never happened. When Seth Merle failed to return Richard Hagopian's money, the dispute reached court. Merle later filed another lawsuit over the same trees, arguing they remained dangerous. The Michigan Court of Appeals dismissed his case, ruling that the issue had already been decided.
